title: Larger Arial text and Wikipedia readability in eye-tracking study
statement:
In an eye-tracking study of Wikipedia, larger Arial text improved objective readability and comprehension was significantly better at 18pt and 26pt than at smaller sizes, supporting 18–26pt as evidence-based options for text-heavy reading interfaces.

Options:
- Evidence-backed large: 18pt (fits: comfortable, editorial)
- More spacious: 20pt (fits: friendly, access-first)
- Reading mode: 22pt (fits: editorial, minimal)
- Maximum tested: 26pt (fits: access-first, reading mode)
appliesWhen: Applies to: content sites, documentation, knowledge bases, web apps. Audience: adults, general.

source.title: Make It Big!: The Effect of Font Size and Line Spacing on Online Readability
source.authors: Luz Rello; Martin Pielot; Mari-Carmen Marcos
source.venue: Proceedings of the 2016 CHI Conference on Human Factors in Computing Systems
